questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How Olympic athletes train and eat before big events
Whether companies selling unhealthy food should sponsor sport
Why skateboarding was added to the Olympic Games
How to cook healthy food at home instead of eating fast food
questions.why: Sam says they'll ask whether it's right for companies selling unhealthy products to sponsor sporting events.

questions.q: What happened to tobacco advertising in 2005?
options: It moved from TV to the internet
It was allowed again at the Olympics
It was replaced by sugary drink adverts
It was banned from international sport
questions.why: Sam says tobacco advertising was banned from international sport in 2005 because smoking is harmful.

questions.q: What was Dr Sandro Demaio's job before he started his own agency?
options: He worked on obesity for the World Health Organisation
He was the team doctor for Australia's Olympic swimmers
He made health programmes for the BBC in London
He advised a fast food company on its advertising
questions.why: He worked for the World Health Organisation specialising in obesity before starting his agency in Australia.

questions.q: According to Dr Demaio, what can a child learn when a fast food brand appears next to a sports hero?
options: That sports stars should not eat fast food
That fast food is cheap and quick
That fast food is connected with success
That they should do more sport
questions.why: He says a young child builds the connection that 'fast food equals success'.

questions.q: What is the other effect of this sponsorship, according to Dr Demaio?
options: People believe the product can't be that bad for them
People stop trusting the sports team that takes the money
People buy fewer tickets for sporting events on television
People become loyal to many different brands at the same time
questions.why: It gives a 'health halo', so people think, even subconsciously, that it can't be that bad.

questions.q: Why do the presenters mention the costs of travel, training and equipment?
options: To show that the Olympics are too expensive for cities
To argue that fast food companies spend too little
To explain why tickets to the Olympics cost so much
To explain why many athletes need sponsorship money
questions.why: Sam says being an athlete can cost a lot with little financial help, so many athletes are desperate for sponsorship.

questions.q: How does Dr Demaio describe ultra-processed foods?
options: As foods that are cooked slowly at home
As natural foods with nothing added
More like products made in a laboratory than real food
As healthy foods that are just high in sugar
questions.why: He says they're 'more products really than foods' and are made in a laboratory, not a kitchen.

questions.q: In Neil's potato example, which one is ultra-processed?
options: A raw potato
French fries
A baked potato
A potato grown without chemicals
questions.why: Neil says a potato is natural, a baked potato is processed, and French fries are ultra-processed.
